summary: Simo Parpola is a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Helsinki (1961–1968) while also studying at the Pontifical Biblical Institute and British Museum. He held posts at Helsinki, Heidelberg, and the University of Chicago.

Simon P. James works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He taught Colette Sciberras and has held posts at Durham University, including philosophy tutor (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Singhathon Narasabho works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Visva-Bharati University under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

Siniruddha Dash is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014) and held directorships at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and K. V. Sarma Research Foundation.

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, the University of London under Frank Raymond Allchin, and Harvard University. He served as Director General of the Department of Archaeology (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He held a professorship at the Indian Statistical Institute and a post at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, both attested in 2009.
Sister Vajirā (1928–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Paul Debes and traditional teacher Narada Maha Thera (1955).
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

So Takahashi (1938–) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo. He held posts as associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and professor (attested 1991) at Meijo University.

Sodo Mori (1934–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera. He held professorships at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) and trained under teachers Kodo Sawaki and Eko Hashimoto.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, and trained under Gempo Yamamoto. He taught Robert Baker Aitken, Maurine Stuart, Eido Tai Shimano, and Philip Kapleau.

Sogaku Daiun Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University under numerous teachers. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1911–1923) and taught Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani and Philip Kapleau.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Nihon University. He held a post at Kanagawa University and taught Kōun Yamada.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy after studying at Nihon University and under traditional teachers including Seisetsu Seki. He served as a professor and president of Hanazono University (1978–1982).

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure who studied at the University of Delhi, Cambridge, and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse. He founded Rigpa in 1975.
Sohanwela Pemarathana is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore (attested 2004).

Soiku Shigematsu (1943–) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. In Buddhist studies and literature, he held professorships at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).

Sojo Hirano (1928–2007) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and shika at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996). He taught Sonja Arntzen and Yoel Hoffmann.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tokyo University of the Arts and under Sōkatsu Shaku and Sōen Shaku. He founded the Buddhist Society of America in 1930 and taught Alan Watts.
